title: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit
description: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. The work shall be completed within 730 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed. This acquisition will be procured as an Unrestricted Full and Open Solicitation. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Construction Contract. All responsible Bidders are encouraged to participate. title: Request for Information (RFI) - OCONUS Generator Maintenance
description: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Request for Information (RFI) Outside Continental United States locations (OCONUS) Generator Maintenance 10/15/2026 The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Logistics Management Directorate, is conducting market research to identify contractors capable of providing on-site generator maintenance and testing services at four Outside Continental United States locations (OCONUS). The anticipated requirement may include key personnel, technician labor, specialized tooling, diagnostic instruments, vehicles, materials, consumables, transportation, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, testing, and related generator support services. The OCONUS requirement encompasses generator assets across three distinct island regions, comprising a total of five distinct operation locations: � Caribbean DC Caribbean: Rd.1, Km 25.1, Quebrada Arenas Ward, Caguas, PR 00725 Ponce Warehouse: 1000 Carr 507, Coto Laurel, PR 00780 � Hawaii DC Hawaii: 99-1269 Iwaena Street, Aiea, HI 96701 East Range: 1980 Higgins Road, Bldg. 6043, Wahiawa, HI 96786 � Guam DC Guam Bldg. 100, Barriagada GU 96913 This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify sources that can provide support for the LMD Outside Continental United States Generator Maintenance (OCONUS Generator Maintenance). In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. Respondents shall identify any proprietary information in their RFI response. Information submitted in response to this RFI will be used at the discretion of the Government. Further, the information submitted will remain confidential insofar as permitted by law, including the Freedom of Information and Privacy Acts. FEMA reserves the right to utilize any non-proprietary technical information in the anticipated PWS or solicitation. Although it is not necessary to address in their response, respondents shall be aware of any potential, actual, or perceived organizational conflicts of interest. Any real or potential conflicts must be sufficiently mitigated prior to a contract award. For further guidance, refer to the Federal Acquisition Regulation, Subpart 3.12 NAICS CODE: 811310 PRODUCT SERVICE CODE (PSC): J061, Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment: Electric Wire, and Power and Distribution Equipment ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE START DATE: 06/30/2027 ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION STRATEGY: To be determined based on market research results ATTACHMENT: OCONUS Generator Inventory Summary October 2026 (.xlsx) Interested contractors shall submit their RFI responses electronically to Oneko Dunbar, Contracting Officer, at Oneko.Dunbar@fema.dhs.gov and Marcia Irizarry-Snyder, Contract Specialist at Marcia.Irizarrysnyder@fema.dhs.gov no later than 11:00 am Eastern Time (ET) November 5, 2026. Questions regarding this RFI are due no later than 11:00 am ET October 21, 2026.

title: Upgrade X-Ray Controller
description: The 76 CMXG is requesting the utilization of funds for the procurement of Upgrade Xray controller and Automated Equipment. In accordance with AIR FORCE T.O 33B-1-2 (Table 3, Master List of Suppo1t Equipment), the system must be an approved equivalent to the X-Ray Apparatus Set (Master/Procmement NSN: MIL-PRF-32133/6635-01-394-5926). The required system must strictly adhere to the following component specifications: SYSTEM SPECIFICATIONS (Upgrade X-ray booth X-ray controller and automated equipment) � Hardware: Includes new servo motors, drives, operator control user interfaces, and manual controls hardware. � Software: Features programmable motion control software based on Parker Motion Systems libraries. title: Annual Preventative Maintenance and Service Support for Seven (7) Miltenyi CliniMACS Prodigy Instruments
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC), Department of Transfusion Medicine (DTM), Center for Cellular Engineering (CCE), intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Miltenyi Biotec, Inc. for annual preventative maintenance and service support of seven (7) CliniMACS Prodigy automated cell-processing instruments, Serial Numbers 0327, 611, 1223, 1326, 1415, 1855, and 917006. Period of Performance: December 1, 2026 � November 30, 2027 These instruments are critical to the manufacture of cell-based therapies for patients participating in clinical trials at the NIH Clinical Center. The equipment operates within Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-regulated Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) facilities and must be maintained in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, including 21 CFR 211.63 and 21 CFR 211.67. The required services include annual preventative maintenance, calibration, software updates and patches, inspections, diagnostic testing, troubleshooting, repair support, replacement of proprietary service parts, and technical support necessary to maintain validated operating conditions. The contractor shall provide preventative maintenance reports for each instrument for review and acceptance by the CCE Quality Assurance team. Sole-Source Authority and Justification The Government intends to procure these services on a sole-source basis pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) and Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Miltenyi Biotec, Inc. is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the CliniMACS Prodigy instruments and the only known authorized source capable of providing the required preventative maintenance, calibration, software support, and repair services. The CliniMACS Prodigy instruments are proprietary systems requiring manufacturer-specific diagnostic tools, software access, replacement parts, and specialized technical expertise. Market research conducted by the Government identified no alternative sources possessing the necessary proprietary rights, manufacturer authorization, software access, and technical capabilities to perform the required services. The instruments have been qualified and incorporated into validated manufacturing processes supporting patient-specific cellular therapies. Utilizing an unauthorized service provider could compromise equipment qualification, disrupt manufacturing operations, increase regulatory compliance risks, and require extensive and costly requalification activities. Such disruptions could adversely affect ongoing clinical trials and patient treatment schedules. Accordingly, Miltenyi Biotec, Inc. has been identified as the only responsible source capable of satisfying the Government's requirements without jeopardizing validated manufacturing processes, operational readiness, and continuity of patient care. Capability Statement Submission This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, all responsible sources that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a written capability statement for consideration. Interested parties must provide sufficient documentation demonstrating their technical capability to perform the required services, including evidence of: Manufacturer authorization to service and maintain Miltenyi CliniMACS Prodigy instruments. Access to proprietary diagnostic software, service tools, technical documentation, and OEM replacement parts. Demonstrated experience performing preventative maintenance, calibration, and repairs on CliniMACS Prodigy instruments. Ability to maintain equipment qualification and compliance with FDA-regulated cGMP manufacturing requirements. Ability to provide required maintenance documentation and technical support without disrupting ongoing clinical manufacturing operations. All capability statements must be received no later than November 5, 2026, at 11:30 AM EST. Responses received after the specified deadline may not be considered. Government Determination The Government will evaluate all timely capability statements received in response to this notice. A determination not to compete this proposed acquisition, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted.

title: Germany – Planting and maintenance services of green areas – Planting of Seagrass for Ostwind 3 Offshore project between KP18.1-18.4
description: The main target for this operation is the planting of seagrass, either as a single plant or/and as a rope consisting plants. Employer is requesting the Bidder to submit a quotation for the execution of seagrass planting works. The designated location for the seagrass planting is at Ostwind 3 cable route between KP18.1 – 18.4, which is a 325m long and 7m wide (about 2300m²) corridor. Seagrass planting will require the following pre-requisites and follow-ups: A consolidated coarse sediment layer of approx. 20 - 30 cm thickness (engineered material), An execution plan, prepared early enough to achieve the permit in time A permit by authorities (STALU VP, WSA Ostsee), Sufficient plant material seagrass shoots (subject to availability, see details below) to be suitable for planting a harbor nearby (either Thiessow (8km), Freest (11km) or Lubmin (15km)) shall be used for hand-over of seagrass shoots/geotextile ropes with seagrass from Third Party supplier In case it is required the work area per operational day shall be first marked by rods/subsurface buoys attached to small ground weights prior to planting to allow for correct planting spatially and regarding shoot density/m². In case of non-fins-diving solutions it can be done different. shifting of work site day by day shall be enabled by installation of a remote-controlled sub-surface marker buoy with release system on last position of executed work, respectively work executed on previous days shall be inspected by means of underwater video (ROV or UW-drone) repeatedly General assumptions about the task: Total impact area to be restored will be ~2.300m² Work can be executed by divers in accordance with the requirements of DGUV Regel 101-023. Alternatively work can be executed by ROV, if the Contractor can proof the suitability of the technology by references Seagrass planting shall start (latest) on 1st of June 2027 and has to be completed by 31st of July 2027. Employer considers two alternative planting methods: (1) planting of single shoots (2) Installation of rotable fabric ropes with incorporated shoots Suitable ropes ready for installation will be provided by an assigned manufacturer. Single shoot planting planting is the preferred procedure, but rope installation shall be implemented in parallel too. If you are interested in participating in the described procedure, please contact us by e-mail (andre.forbrig@50hertz.com) and express your interest in participating. With the expression of interest, we need the following information from you in order to be able to add you to the project in Ariba: - Full name of the company: - Address of the company: - V.A.T. Number: - Tax Number: - Commercial register number: In addition, I need the contact details of the people who you should have access to the Ariba system: - Name - E-mail address - Phone number

title: Mode5/TCAS/Surveillance Cloaking Capability
description: 1. Purpose This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research purposes only. The Government is seeking information from capable and interested businesses, including small businesses, that can provide systems engineering support for integration and test of Mode 5, Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS), and surveillance cloaking capability into two United States Marine Corps (USMC) Boeing C-40A Clipper aircraft. This notice is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, invitation for bid, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Information received will be used to assess the availability of qualified sources, determine the extent of small-business capability, and inform the Government�s acquisition strategy. 2. Requirement Description The Government anticipates a requirement for systems engineering, avionics integration, and test support associated with incorporation of surveillance capability into two USMC Boeing C-40A Clipper aircraft. The anticipated place of performance is Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland. Additional travel or support at other Government or contractor locations may be required, as identified in any future solicitation or statement of work. The anticipated effort includes engineering analysis, integration planning, interface assessment, configuration management, installation support, ground- and flight-test planning and execution, anomaly resolution, technical-data development, and technical program support. The effort requires integration of the following avionics equipment: APX-119-540 Transponder � P/N 4079100-0540 Digital Control Panel (DCP) � P/N 4087561-0503 KIV-79 Crypto Applique � P/N 4079080-0503 Personality Module (PM) � P/N 4088953-0501 TPA-100B Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) Computer � P/N 940-0351-010 3. Anticipated Scope Potential sources should be capable of providing the following, as applicable: Review and analyze aircraft-level, system-level, and equipment-level requirements. description: This Special Notice is to advise intrested memeber of the Training and Readiness Accelerator II (TREX II), as well as other intrested members within the U.S technology base, that a Request for Solutions (RFS) has been issued by Advanced Technology International (ATI) to develop a training device of the 120mm Mortar Training Sytem. The purpose the Training Readiness and Aceelerator (TREX II) is to spur innovative development, demonstration, and expedited delivery of prototypes to increase Warefighter readiness via modeling, simulation, education/ training, expermental validation, and miltary readiness focued projects. A constorium has been establised to develop prototypes presonnel and the support the platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DoD) or to improvement of platforms, systems, components of materials in use by the Armed Forces. Link for TREX II- https://www/trexii.org/ Objectives:STE LTS is seeking a training system for 120mm mortars in both the Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicle (AMPV) and Stryker M1129 Mortar Carrier that: 1. title: Marine Corps Acquisition Exchange (MCAX) Hosted by Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC), Headquarters Marine Corps Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L), and Including Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Information Tec
description: When: Thursday, 19 November 2026, 9:30 a.m. EST. The event will last approximately four hours. Where: Join us in person or virtually via Microsoft Teams. During registration, industry partners will be asked to indicate their preferred method of attendance (in person or virtual). Because venue capacity is limited, requesting in-person attendance does not guarantee an in-person invitation. In-person attendance will be limited to two representatives per entity. Invitations will generally be issued in registration order, subject to venue capacity and Government discretion, including consideration for first-time attendees. After registration closes, confirmed in-person attendees and virtual participants will receive the appropriate access information by email. Registration Closes: 5 Nov 2026 Ready to join us? Register using the link below. Please copy and paste the link into your browser rather than attempting to access it directly through SAM.gov: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/Cx4WtRHSKa If you experience issues with the registration link, please contact us at: SMB_PAE_MC_CTIndustry@usmc.mil One quick favor before you hit submit: Please double-check your email address and telephone number. Your invitation and event information will be sent using the contact information you provide during registration. An incorrect email address means we will not be able to get your invitation to you. In the event of unforeseen technical issues, the virtual session may be cancelled. If that happens, presentation materials will be provided to registered attendees following the event. BACKGROUND Let�s Talk About What�s Next. Good acquisition starts with communication. Not just when a solicitation hits SAM.gov. Not just when proposals are due. And certainly not only after we already know exactly what we want to buy. Sometimes the most valuable conversation happens much earlier. On 19 November 2026, Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) and Headquarters Marine Corps Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L) invite industry to join us for our next quarterly Marine Corps Acquisition Exchange (MCAX). Together with the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) Information Technology Contracting Center (ITCC) and other Marine Corps acquisition and requirements stakeholders, we want to give industry a clearer look at where we're headed�and an opportunity to talk with the people helping us get there. The 19 November MCAX will provide industry with visibility into anticipated contracting opportunities across participating Marine Corps organizations, while creating dedicated time for questions and direct Government�Industry engagement. What are we looking for? Ideas. Capabilities. Competition. Innovation. And, most importantly, meaningful dialogue with industry partners who understand that supporting the Marine Corps begins with understanding the mission. Our senior leaders, Capability Portfolio Managers, acquisition professionals, PAE MC Rapid Capability Cell (RCC) representatives, and Small Business experts will share information about emerging requirements, acquisition priorities, and anticipated contracting opportunities across the Marine Corps enterprise. And we don't want the conversation to go only one way. MCAX is also our opportunity to hear from you. What are you seeing in the marketplace? Where is technology moving? What capabilities already exist that we should know about? And where can better communication between Government and Industry help us find smarter ways to meet the needs of the warfighter? That exchange matters. Because when Government better understands what industry can deliver�and industry better understands where the Marine Corps is going�we can have better conversations about how to get there. Whether you've supported the Marine Corps for decades, you're an innovative small business looking for your first opportunity, or you're somewhere in between, you're invited to be part of that conversation. Come hear what we're working on. Ask questions. Engage with the people behind the requirements. And gain a clearer understanding of where your capabilities may align with what comes next. EVENT FORMAT We know your time is valuable. That's why we're continuing to focus MCAX on the information and engagement that industry has told us matters most. The approximately four-hour live event is anticipated to include: Briefs from leaders in Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC), Headquarters Marine Corps, Installations & Logistics (HQMC I&L), Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS), PAE MC Cyber Technology Office, PAE MC RCC, and the Combat Development & Integration (CD&I) Capability Portfolio Managers (CPMs) Contract Opportunity Briefs from PAE MC, HQMC I&L and PAE MS Information Technology Contracting Center (ITCC) Industry Q&A We will continue streamlining formal presentations wherever possible so there is more time for meaningful engagement between Industry and Government. And because showing up prepared makes for a better conversation, we're giving you a head start. Before MCAX, take some time to explore the PAE MC Industry Portal at: https://www.pae.marines.mil/industry-portal/ The portal is designed to help industry learn more about PAE MC, our mission, and how to engage with us before the conversation begins. Have a capability we should know about? Industry partners are encouraged to submit capability briefs or white papers through the Industry Portal before the event. Sharing that information in advance gives our team an opportunity to better understand what you bring to the table and where your capabilities may connect with Marine Corps needs. A preview of selected contracting opportunities associated with the 19 November MCAX will also be added to this notice as soon as it becomes available. Industry partners are encouraged to check this notice periodically for updates prior to the event, review the opportunities in advance, and come ready to engage. HQMC I&L opportunities will be released to industry within five business days following the event through a separate SAM.gov announcement. One Mission. Many Opportunities. One Conversation Worth Having. We hope you'll join us on 19 November.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Isle au Haut Thoroughfare near Isle au Haut, Maine
description: The Isle au Haut Thoroughfare Federal Navigation Project, located between Isle au Haut, Maine and Kimball Island, Maine on the outskirts of Penobscot Bay, about six miles southeast of Stonington and 25 miles east of Rockland. The Federal Navigation Project consists of a -6-foot Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) deep by 75-foot wide extending 1,200-foot in length through the shoal in the thoroughfare.The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,355 cubic yards (cy) (1,183 cy required, plus 2,172 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting of highly compacted coarse sand and gravel, with areas of cobbles and isolated small boulders from the channel. Due to the material type, a mechanical dredge with the ability to dig highly compacted coarse sand and gravel will be required. The proposed action is to dredge to the authorized depth of -6-foot MLLW plus an additional 1-foot of required advance maintenance with an additional allowable 1-foot of overdepth (e.g. -7-foot MLLW required + 1-foot allowable OD). One-time, advanced maintenance is approved for the entirety of the 1200-foot long authorized channel. The dredged material will be placed at the Flake Island Disposal Site (FIDS) which is approximately 1 nautical mile northwest of the FNP. Placement of the dredged material (sand, gravel and cobble) at Flake Island Disposal Site will benefit both juvenile lobster habitat and juvenile cod by increasing the areas habitat complexity.The anticipated allowable dredging window is between September 15 and April 1 to avoid impacts to spawning shellfish, benthic resources, Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) of federally managed species, threatened and endangered species and interactions with mobile fishing gear.

title: CMT Catered Meals
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation, quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation is being issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 dated 13 Mar 2026. This solicitation number W91ZRS27QA001 is for the Connecticut Army National Guard (CTARNG). The USPFO for Connecticut intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price contract for CMT Catered Meals. This request is due by 03 November 2026 at 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time). This solicitation is 100% small business set aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 311991 � (Perishable Prepared Food Manufacturing). The small business standard size for NAICS 311991 is 700 employees. Instructions to Offerors All questions shall be in writing. Questions may be faxed to Leslie Fedler at 860-386-4070 or emailed at leslie.a.fedler.civ@army.mil. Questions must be submitted No Later Than 30 October 2026. All quotes are due no later than 1:00 p.m. eastern time, 03 November 2026. Quotes may be faxed to Leslie Fedler at 860-386-4070 or emailed to leslie.a.fedler.civ@army.mil. It is your responsibility to make sure your quote is received. The fact that the contracting office did not receive your quote due to an error on the fax machine or email address does not change the due date or time. Basis for Award "The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Award will be made on an 'all or none' basis to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offeror. Tradeoffs will not be permitted. Quotes will be evaluated for technical acceptability, past performance acceptability, and price." Evaluation Process: "The Government intends to evaluate quotes by first sorting them from lowest price to highest price. The lowest-priced quote will then be evaluated for technical acceptability and past performance. If the lowest-priced quote is determined to be 'Technically Acceptable' and has 'Acceptable Past Performance,' award will be made to that offeror, and no further quotes will be evaluated." Factor 1: Technical Acceptability: "The technical quote will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis. To be rated Acceptable, the quote must clearly demonstrate a compliance approach that meets all requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS), specifically demonstrating the capability to distribute media across the required channels and networks." Factor 2: Past Performance: "Past Performance will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. To be rated Acceptable, the offeror must submit a minimum of two (2) references within the past three (3) years demonstrating similar scope, complexity, and NAICS 311991 relevance. Offerors with no relevant past performance history will receive a 'Neutral' rating, which will be treated as 'Acceptable' for award purposes." Factor 3: Price: "Price will be evaluated for mathematical completeness and price reasonableness. Award will be made to the lowest total priced, responsible offeror whose technical and past performance quotes are rated Acceptable." The Contracting Officer will evaluate products on the basis of information furnished by the offeror or identified in the offer and reasonably available to the Contracting Officer. The Contracting Officer is not responsible for locating or obtaining any information not identified in the offer. The Government is not responsible for developing the comparison from insufficient information provided. Must be Technical Acceptability" as meeting both the performance capability and statutory compliance with FAR 52.219-30 and 13 CFR 125.6. Sam�s Registration: Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database before an award can be made to them. If the offeror is not registered in the SAM, they may do so through the SAM website at http://www.sam.gov. Payment shall be paid thru the wide area workflow program. All payments are net 30 days. All Offerors must accept this as payment. The wide area workflow website is https://wawf.eb.mil/. The Government contract supersedes all other terms and agreements from any other vendor. The only award will be from the Government. SERVICE CONTRACT LABOR STANDARDS (SCLS) This solicitation and resulting contract are subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute . Contractors must pay all covered employees performing under this contract no less than the minimum wages and fringe benefits outlined in the attached U.S. Department of Labor Wage Determination No. 2015-4113 REV 37 . The primary labor category utilized under this contract is identified as: SCA Labor Category: Driver SCA Occupational Code: 31043 - Driver Courier Offerors are responsible for ensuring that their proposed labor rates comply fully with the wage and health/welfare benefits specified in the attached Wage Determination . Performance Work Statement 1.0 SCOPE This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the requirements for a non-personal services contract to provide complete dining facility (DFAC) and meal services for the United States Army. The Contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control to perform the full scope of food services as defined herein, with the exception of government-furnished property and services. 2.0 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS The Contractor shall perform complete food services and meet the performance standards set forth in this document. All services will be performed in strict accordance with all applicable local, county, state, and federal regulations, as well as military-specific guidelines, including but not limited to the Tri-Service Food Code (TB MED 530) and Army Regulation (AR) 30-22. Contract can be terminated if it is determined to not meet the needs of the Military unit being serviced. 2.1 Pricing and Payment Terms: The contractor shall provide a detailed pricing structure based on the following: � Cost per meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner). � Total meal count per day will vairy throughout the course (see Annex A) � Payment terms (e.g., weekly invoicing, net 30 days). 3.0 COORDINATION AND LOGISTICS 3.1 Adherence to Meal and Strength Schedule: The Government will provide a Meal Service and Strength Schedule (attached as Annex A). This schedule will detail the required mealtimes and the exact personnel count for each meal service (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) for the entire period of performance. The Contractor must strictly adhere to the specified times and headcounts listed in this schedule for all meal preparations and deliveries. The final invoice must match the numbers specified in this calendar. Any deviation not pre-approved in writing may result in non-payment for the excess meals provided. Delivery times for meals are referenced in Annex A 169th RTI 1st Quarter Course Meal Plan FY27. The timeline for meals is as follows unless otherwise annotated: Breakfast: 0700-0800, Lunch 1200-1245, Dinner 1700-1745. 3.2 Meal Order Modifications: All requests for changes to meal quantities or meal types must be submitted by the designated Government Point of Contact (POC) to the contractor via email or text message. No changes will be accepted by the contractor any later than 72 hours prior to the scheduled meal delivery time. This 72-hour deadline is firm and ensures the contractor has adequate time for procurement and preparation. The contractor is not obligated to accommodate requests made after this deadline. 3.3 Singular Drop-off Location:

description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE The United States Air Force (the Government) intends to issue a Firm-Fixed-Price order to a single source; immixTechnology, Inc, on or about 16 November 2026. The period of performance is expected to run for 12 months. PSC: 7A21 NAICS: 513210 Size Standard: $47M Product Name / Type: Patran Software Supplier Name: Hexagon Manufacturing Intelligence, Inc. / immixTechnology, Inc. Product Description: Patran is the world's most widely used pre/post-processing software for Finite Element Analysis (FEA), providing solid modeling, meshing, analysis setup and post-processing for multiple solvers including MSC Nastran, Marc, Abaqus, LS-DYNA, ANSYS, and Pam-Crash. Patran provides a rich set of tools that streamline the creation of analysis ready models for linear, nonlinear, explicit dynamics, thermal, and other finite element solutions. Responses are limited to 10 pages in a Microsoft Word compatible format. Responses should be emailed to Shelby Sartin at Shelby.Sartin.1@us.af.mil no later than, 05 November 2026, 1:00 PM EST. Any questions should be directed to Shelby Sartin through email.

description: Presolicitation Notice to Single Source Solicitation Number: W9127N27Q1CTI Agency: Department of the Army Office: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Location: USACE District, Portland Classification Code: F022 � Natural Resources/Conservation�Fish Hatchery NAICS Code: 112511 - Finfish Farming and Fish Hatcheries Notice Type: Presolicitation Notice Synopsis: This is a special notice prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO FAR) 5.101 �Presolicitation Notice� The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Portland District (NWP) intends to negotiate/award a sole source contract with the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation (Yakama Nation). All requirements necessary will be provided for the annual acclimation and release of up to 1.1 million sub-yearling upriver bright (URB) fall Chinook juveniles (received from Little White Salmon Hatchery) and for an additional 210 thousand yearling URB fall Chinook juveniles (received from Bonneville Hatchery) at Prosser Hatchery; releases are expected to occur from May through June at 75 to 50 fish per pound and from March through April at 20 fish per pound, respectively. Additionally, Portland District will require Yakama Nation (YN) to supply 600,000 Upriver Bright (URB) Fall Chinook smolts (sourced entirely by Yakama Nation) to be released into the Yakima River from Prosser Hatchery at river mile 46.8; releases are expected to occur from May through June at fish sizes of 75 to 50 fish per pound. This fish production satisfies a portion of USACE�s mission in fulfilling mitigation obligations for The Dalles and John Day Dams. Pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2304(c)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1 and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation (DFARS) 206.302-1, only one responsible source and no other vendor will satisfy agency requirements. In 2008, the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) issued a revised Biological Opinion that concluded that the Federal Columbia River Power System jeopardizes the continued existence of various Endangered Species Act-listed anadromous fish in the Columbia River Basin. Jeopardy and adverse modification may be avoided by implementing reasonable and prudent alternatives (RPAs) composed of discrete actions covering, among other things, hatchery operations. RPA action number 40 calls for a review of the hatchery program associated with the mitigation for The Dalles and John Day Dams. After reviewing the program, USACE, among other agencies and organizations, ultimately arrived at a plan to move the hatchery operations into or above the exclusive Zone 6 Indian fishery to better meet mitigation objectives. Prosser Hatchery is situated just downstream of Prosser Dam at river kilometer 75 of the Yakima River. The Yakima River feeds into the Columbia River near Richland, Washington, above Zone 6. Prosser Hatchery possesses the appropriate water temperature, rearing pond space and availability during the required months to acclimate and release the subject fall Chinook juveniles into the Yakima River. No other acclimation and release facilities exist in, or near, the lower Yakima River that are 1) capable of acclimating these fish, and 2) not already in use by USACE for similar purposes. The underlying land, facilities and equipment at Prosser Hatchery are under the ownership of the Yakama Nation. Therefore, Yakama Nation has sole control and use of the facilities at Prosser Hatchery and does not permit other contractors to utilize these facilities. Regional fisheries experts from NMFS, USFWS and USACE agree that Prosser Hatchery is the only reasonable location to perform these specific rearing and release activities. The statutory authority for this non-competitive acquisition 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FRO FAR 6.103-1 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 206.103-170, there is only one responsible source, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. A SOLICITATION WILL NOT BE POSTED The Government intends to proceed with this sole source action. The NAICS code is 112511, Finfish Farming and Hatcheries. The size standard as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration is $3.75 million. title: GAOA Grizzly Bear Campground
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 127EAX27Q0004 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for updates to the Grizzly Bear Campground. Updates include: Road alignment will be adjusted to accommodate expected traffic, subbase will be enhanced. The water system well will remain; the pumphouse, service and distribution lines, and point-of-use hydrants will be replaced and rerouted to better serve campers. The information board will be replaced and relocated. Host and Volunteer Sites will each to be equipped with sewage vault, water, and electric services. Campsites will be redesigned for accessibility and improved layout, parking and functionality. A new stick-built double toilet and stick-built pump house are part of the project. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

The proposed project consists of turnkey removal and replacement of two existing utility feed transformers at the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Fish Dispersal Barrier facility in Lockport, Illinois. title: Y1DA--VISN 2 EHRM Industry Day
description: Construction Industry Day Introduction In accordance with FAR Companion (FC) 10.001(c), this notice is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), nor will the VA pay for information requested. Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) will host an industry day event at the James J. Peters Department of Veterans Affairs VA Medical Center (VAMC), located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468 for all businesses (including, but not limited to, general contractors, subcontractor trades, and material suppliers) interested in the upcoming Electronic Health Records Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades construction projects throughout VISN 2 (NY/NJ). The purpose of the Industry Day is to facilitate collaboration between the VA and general construction contractors and subcontractors of all business sizes who are interested in performing work in New York and New Jersey. This session is designed to give all interested contractors a clear understanding of the project s intent, performance expectations, and execution approach. This industry day will help the VA determine the method of procurement and type of socioeconomic set-aside, if any, highlight any industry concerns, gauge general contractor interest in the project, and perform a site walk to show key areas of the Bronx EHRM project. Six EHRM Infrastructure projects were solicited and awarded in FY26. Four of the six were designated as SDVOSB set-asides, and most of these projects received limited bids or proposals. In FY27, VISN 2 anticipates three projects, Bronx, Manhattan, and Northport, that are particularly large and complex, which may pose significant challenges for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) to execute independently due to their scale and technical requirements. As a result, the VA is considering broadening the competition beyond SDVOSBs, seeking participation from both small and/or large businesses that have the project experience, capabilities, and workforce necessary to fulfill the contract demands. This approach is critical to ensuring a robust competitive environment that accurately reflects market value and supports successful project delivery. EVENT INFORMATION The industry day will be held on Thursday, November 19th, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM ET. The meeting location will be Room 3D-22 in Building 100, located at 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468. Contractors are required to pre-register for this event. See Administrative section below. Proposed Agenda: 1. Check-in (please arrive between 9 - 9:30 AM) 2. Introductions 3. Meet and Greet 4. Overview of the EHRM Program and Each Project 4. Site walk of the Bronx VAMC EHRM project 5. Lunch Break 6. Questions and answers session 7. Networking *A final agenda will most likely be posted to SAM.gov closer to the event date. PROJECT DESCRIPTIONS VISN 2 (New York/New Jersey) has five EHRM projects that are anticipated to be solicited and awarded in Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 and four in FY 2028. The five planned locations for FY27 are at the following VAMC s: Bronx, Canandaigua, Manhattan, Northport, and St. Albans. A description of each project is listed below. Bronx VAMC: The design modernizes the campus technology backbone and supporting building systems so the medical center can implement the VA EHRM platform while maintaining reliable clinical and facility operations. Work extends across the Main Hospital (Building 100) and multiple adjacent campus buildings and support facilities. A distinguishing feature is the construction of two new telecommunications towers. The towers expand communications capacity and require coordinated architectural, structural, civil, electrical, mechanical, and telecommunications design. The broader project also renovates and expands existing telecommunications and data center spaces and upgrades the supporting power, cooling, fiber, security, and life-safety infrastructure. Canandaigua VAMC: This project comprehensively upgrades the campus s fiber optic network and power distribution systems to meet EHRM design guide requirements, ensuring robust support for clinical and facility operations. The work encompasses fiber network enhancements with redundant routes to each IT closet and the main demarcation room, minimizing risk through parallel systems operation during transitions from legacy to new infrastructure. The project also includes expansion or relocation of telecommunications rooms, installation of 100 new IT outlets and 75 electrical outlets, and substantial improvements in power distribution and HVAC systems. Enhanced physical security is provided through secure data cabinets, protected fiber infrastructure, secured telecommunications rooms, and installation of lockable manhole covers for underground fiber pathways. In addition, hazardous material abatement activities will ensure that all upgraded spaces meet current safety and environmental standards. Manhattan VAMC: The design modernizes telecommunications and IT infrastructure throughout Buildings 1, 2, 3, and 6 and creates resilient power and cooling systems to support continuous healthcare operations and future technology demands. The project relocates the existing data center to renovated space and upgrades 53 telecommunications rooms and enclosures. The new data center functions as the campus telecommunications hub and is supported by redundant fiber pathways, dedicated year-round cooling, and 2N UPS and electrical distribution redundancy. These features distinguish the Manhattan project and increase the reliability of critical IT systems. Northport VAMC: This information will be provided in an update to this posting on SAM.gov. St. Albans VAMC: The EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Project at St. Albans VA Medical Center in Queens, NY, is a large-scale modernization effort designed to support the implementation of the VA s new EHRM system. The initiative involves major upgrades across multiple buildings, including the construction of a new data center and telecom tower, extensive electrical and mechanical improvements, and the installation of advanced technology infrastructure such as Cat 6A cabling and a fiber optic backbone, all guided by strict VA standards for compliance, safety, and scalability. Key challenges include managing hazardous materials like asbestos and lead-based paint, addressing spatial and technical constraints in existing telecom rooms, coordinating complex system upgrades within an active healthcare environment, and ensuring meticulous phasing to minimize disruptions. Additionally, the project must integrate diverse building systems, adhere to evolving standards, and provide future-proofing for anticipated growth, all of which add significant complexity to both the design and execution phases. *The following projects anticipated for award in FY28: Albany, Buffalo, Batavia and East Orange. Procurement Information The proposed projects will be a competitive firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (final specifications and drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued as either request for proposals (RFP) in accordance with FAR part 15, considering technical and price factors or Invitation for Bids (IFBs) in accordance with FAR part 14, considering price only. The full acquisition strategy for this proposed project has not yet been developed and will be determined after the industry day and any additional market research is concluded. The targeted cost ranges of each project are listed below. Between $20 and $30 Million: Canandaigua and St. Albans Between $40 and $50 Million: Bronx and Manhattan Between $50 and $60 Million: Northport The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45 million. title: Countermeasures That Work (CMTW) Updates
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) maintains Countermeasures That Work, an evidence-based reference guide used by State Highway Safety Offices (SHSOs) and other stakeholders to identify effective behavioral traffic safety countermeasures. NHTSA is seeking contractor support to update the guide based on the latest available research, emerging countermeasures, and developments in highway safety. The purpose of this requirement is to update the current 12th edition of Countermeasures That Work and its electronic version (E-CMTW), resulting in the 13th edition. The contractor will conduct comprehensive literature searches, review and evaluate relevant research, and incorporate significant new findings, resources, and implementation considerations into approximately three to four program-area chapters annually. The final deliverable will include a consolidated Word document incorporating all updates made during the period of performance.

title: Countermeasures That Work (CMTW) Updates
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) maintains Countermeasures That Work, an evidence-based reference guide used by State Highway Safety Offices (SHSOs) and other stakeholders to identify effective behavioral traffic safety countermeasures. NHTSA is seeking contractor support to update the guide based on the latest available research, emerging countermeasures, and developments in highway safety. The purpose of this requirement is to update the current 12th edition of Countermeasures That Work and its electronic version (E-CMTW), resulting in the 13th edition. The contractor will conduct comprehensive literature searches, review and evaluate relevant research, and incorporate significant new findings, resources, and implementation considerations into approximately three to four program-area chapters annually. The final deliverable will include a consolidated Word document incorporating all updates made during the period of performance.

description: The Department of Commerce (DOC), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS), Office of Satellite and Product Operations (OSPO) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract with a magnitude ranging from $7M to $10M to ATLAS Space Operations Inc., (UEI: LUU8R95P3JM3). The requirement is to procure scalable telemetry, tracking and command aperture services to deliver Satellite-to-Ground Communication Services. This requirement supports OSPO in accomplishing its mission of delivering environmental data from remote platforms. The scope encompasses site certification, telemetry downlink data services, and satellite commanding data services to satisfy future NESDIS requirements for commercial remote telemetry downlink for partner missions. Key supported missions include, but are not limited to: COSMIC-2, (the Constellation Observing System for Meteorology Ionosphere and Climate-2)/FORMOSAT-7 KOMPSAT-5, Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite-5 (KOMPSAT-5), and PAZ, Spanish Earth Observation Satellite The proposed contract action will be conducted using other than full and open competition procedures pursuant to the authority at 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 6.103-1,Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services will satisfy agency requirements. Justification for Non-Competitive Action: ATLAS is the only vendor that possesses the established, fully compliant ground station network and operational authorizations required to fulfill NOAA's mission objectives without catastrophic schedule disruption and unrecoverable cost growth. ATLAS currently holds all active, validated, and fully compliant international spectrum licenses and host-nation operating authorizations across the required equatorial downlink footprint. These authorizations are non-transferable. ATLAS represents the only evaluated source possessing the fully qualified, operational front-end processor architectures, automated scheduling APIs, and verified performance thresholds required to meet NESDIS data delivery requirements without introducing unacceptable integration costs, programmatic delays, and mission-critical data loss risks. However, in accordance with RFO 5.101, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. title: AF-PLM Capability Integration, Sustainment & Licenses
description: The United States Air Force (USAF) has implemented an Enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) solution to modernize the management of weapon systems throughout their lifecycle. This initiative aligns with the Air Force's broader strategic goals to integrate capabilities, revolutionize processes, and enable lifecycle digital material management. The current PLM implementation leverages Siemens Teamcenter, a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solution hosted within the Cloud One environment, to empower program offices with centralized, secure, and integrated tools for engineering, manufacturing, sustainment, and asset retirement activities. The USAF continues to face significant challenges in fully realizing seamless PLM integration across its enterprise. These challenges include fragmented legacy systems, disconnected data silos, and a lack of uniformity in processes, all of which contribute to inefficiencies, reduced data integrity, and delays in decision-making. Addressing these issues requires innovative solutions that ensure robust configuration management, streamline workflows, and foster enterprise-wide collaboration while adhering to stringent security and compliance standards. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather industry feedback on technical approaches, market capabilities, and innovative solutions to address these challenges as well as management of licenses required for these capabilities. By engaging with vendors, the USAF seeks to achieve a better understanding of the current state of the market, identify potential pathways for enhancing the AF-PLM capability and license management, and refine its requirements for prospective procurements. Vendor responses will play a critical role in shaping acquisition strategies, identifying feasible solutions, and ensuring that the evolving PLM environment aligns with the USAF's operational and strategic needs. This process supports the overarching goal of achieving an authoritative source of truth for product data and enhancing total lifecycle management for USAF weapon systems. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for Market Research (MR) purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force (AF) is not seeking proposals, nor will it accept unsolicited proposals at this time. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. The information provided may be used by the Air Force in developing its understanding of current market conditions. Interested parties are responsible for marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information contained in their response. Do not submit any classified information in response to this RFI. The Government reserves the right to contact additional customers to obtain information that will be used to evaluate the offeror�s capability. The Government does not plan to respond or conduct formal debriefings to vendors as part of this request. Respondents are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this request. All costs associated with responding to this request will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this request does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued.

Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. title: Countermeasures That Work (CMTW) Updates
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) maintains Countermeasures That Work, an evidence-based reference guide used by State Highway Safety Offices (SHSOs) and other stakeholders to identify effective behavioral traffic safety countermeasures. NHTSA is seeking contractor support to update the guide based on the latest available research, emerging countermeasures, and developments in highway safety. The purpose of this requirement is to update the current 12th edition of Countermeasures That Work and its electronic version (E-CMTW), resulting in the 13th edition. The contractor will conduct comprehensive literature searches, review and evaluate relevant research, and incorporate significant new findings, resources, and implementation considerations into approximately three to four program-area chapters annually. The final deliverable will include a consolidated Word document incorporating all updates made during the period of performance.

The IUID definition at DFARS 211.274-1 says IUID "is a system of marking, valuing and tracking items delivered to DoD." These spares are non-CLSSA FMS assets and will never be delivered to DoD. The assets are delivered to a domestic U.S. freight forwarder who is under contract by the FMS customer to ship the assets to the country of record. The FMS customer countries retain ownership of their parts throughout the asset's lifecycle. These parts will never be owned by the U.S. Government, and will never be entered into the DoD supply chain. Based on this, there is no need for these non-CLSSA FMS country assets to be specially marked for tracking by DoD. \

The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. title: Space Communications and Networking (SCaN) & Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRS) Support
description: NASA/Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources capable of providing engineering team support for Space Communications and Networking (SCaN) specifically focusing on mission?critical Ka?band communications services that ensure continuity of service for users of NASA�s Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System (TDRS). The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) is seeking capability statements from all interested parties, including all socioeconomic categories of Small Businesses (SB) and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU)/Minority Institutions (MI) for the purposes of determining the appropriate level of competition and/or small business subcontracting goals in support of TDRS. Vendors are encouraged to demonstrate capabilities as a prime, subcontractor and/or teaming partner. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), HUBZone, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, and Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) business set-aside based on responses received. Respondents are requested to provide informed input on realistic and appropriate SB subcontracting and/or participation goals for the specific requirement. This type of feedback supports NASA�s market research and helps ensure the acquisition strategy is aligned with actual industry capability. Industry feedback is requested for: 1. SB Subcontracting goals; 2. Barriers that may limit SB participation, such as certifications, unique technical requirements, security needs, specialized tools, or high-risk performance areas and/or 3. Strategies to increase SB participation, including: � Breaking requirements into smaller components � Identifying areas appropriate for subcontracting � Considering teaming or mentor prot�g� approaches This requirement provides critical engineering skills, manpower, and technical capability support for NASA�s mission-critical Ka-band communications; providing continuity of service for TDRS users. The engineering team supporting NASA is required to provide expertise and utilize developed tools and skills to support systems engineering, integration, verification, test, and operations in the deployment of NASA technology. The anticipated period of performance is two (2) years and is anticipated to include fewer than ten Work Year Equivalents (WYEs). All work is expected to be performed on-site at NASA/MSFC. NASA/MSFC seeks information regarding contractor capabilities to provide the TDRS communications services and technical support described herein, including required clearances and experience. Requirement will include the following seven (7) major skill categories in support of TDRS: Materials and Mechanisms Propulsion and Thermal Control Systems Avionics, Power Systems, and Batteries Aerospace Flight Software and Guidance, Navigation, and Control Systems General Software and Infrastructure Systems Hardware Qualifications, Acceptance, and Functional Test Radio Frequency (RF) Communication (Comm) No solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. Interested firms are responsible for monitoring this website for the release of any presolicitation or solicitation notice. Interested parties should submit a capability statement in either Microsoft Word, PowerPoint or PDF format. Files should not be greater than five (5) pages (no less than 12-point font) and contain the following information: Company name, address, point of contact, and business size (e.g., large, small, SB/WOSB/SDVOSB, etc.). Registration with GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) and state whether currently registered and provide contract vehicle information. Any relevant experience to MAS category Special Item Numbers (SIN) 541715 Engineering Research and Development and Strategic Planning. Demonstrate capability to provide personnel to work in a classified environment at the Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) level. All personnel shall maintain a TS/SCI security clearance while supporting any future contract. Also demonstrate verified International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) compliance. Description of relevant experience providing mission?critical TDRS Ka?band communications services specifically identifying any relevant NASA or GSA contract numbers under which work was performed. Any additional information that would assist NASA in understanding industry capability and readiness. All responses must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer, Cynthia Hubbard, at Cynthia.a.hubbard@nasa.gov no later than 4:00 P.M. CST November 5, 2027. Please reference SCaN/TDRS Support in any response. This sources sought notice is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation.

title: Remedial Action (RA) activities at the Kahuku Point Former Radio Range site
description: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) contemplates issuing a Screening Information Request (SIR) for Remedial Action (RA) activities at the Kahuku Point Former Radio Range site (Site), located on the North Shore of Oahu, Hawaii. Activities include excavating 3,768 tons of soil contaminated with lead and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and disposing of the soil offsite according to applicable regulations. The purpose of this pre-solicitation is to solicit statements of interest and capabilities from Small Business Administration (SBA) small business concerns capable of performing the type of work described in this notice. The Contractor will provide all equipment, supplies, labor, transportation, and supervision necessary to perform the tasks described in the scope of work (SOW), not attached. The SOW includes, but is not limited to, the following: - The Contractor must excavate contaminated soil that was identified in reports that will be available at time of solicitation. - The Contractor must arrange for proper storage, transport, and disposal of all investigation-derived waste (IDW) generated from this RA, including necessary sampling for proper disposal. Backfilling of the excavated area will not be required. - Excavation, hauling, and disposal, quantities are as follows: Area to be excavated: 3.2 acres. Average depth of excavation: 1 foot. Average density of excavated soil excavation reports at the site): 0.73 tons per cubic yard. Total tons to be excavated: 3,768 tons. - The Contractor must decommission and remove the five (5) groundwater monitoring wells at the Site. The wells must be decommissioned according to the regulatory requirements of HDOH. The wells are very shallow and will not require the use of a drill rig for removal. - The Contractor must identify all buried utility systems where subsurface work will take place. A request for locate services with the appropriate public utility dig-line for the area must be filed within the required timeline prior to site work. - The Contractor must use GIS to generate the survey coordinates of the perimeters of the DUs to be excavated according to the attached Figure 2. The perimeters of the DUs to be excavated must be located in the field to the horizontal accuracy of 1 foot. - The Contractor is responsible for obtaining all permits and permissions and submitting all notifications required to complete this scope of work. - The Contractor is required to submit pre and post project documentation for this contract. Acceptance of Contractor submittals is subject to the approval of the FAA and other local, state, and federal regulatory agencies as applicable to the specific project. - Confirmation sampling is not required in this solicitation. Any sampling and analysis required for waste characterization purposes must be conducted according to requirements of the facility accepting the waste. In order to better understand the market for this potential requirement, the FAA requests the following information from interested small business vendors (no preference given at this time): 1. Name of Company (the resultant Prime contractor that may ultimately be awarded the subsequent contract) 2. Address 3. Point of Contact name, email address and telephone number 4. UEI Number 5. Relevant experience on similar projects within the last five years. Please provide specific contract numbers, contact names and email information to support claimed capabilities. Please submit your capability statement and the above information to Sonia.o.holguin@faa.gov no later than November 5, 2026 by 1500 Central Daylight Savings Time. Failure to respond to this pre-solicitation with the information requested above will preclude a Contractor�s ability to receive a copy of the future solicitation. Subsequent award will be made on lowest price technically acceptable basis. Limit complete responses to no more than five pages. Information will not be released; however, mark PROPRIETARY on all documents submitted, as applicable. Funds are not currently available for this requirement.

description: Description NOTE: On 07 October 2026, Solicitation Amendment 003 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, and a revised Section L, which are identified in the Amendment summary of changes.
